newsitem.title: SPAIN: Traders think BoS intervening to stop peseta rise.
newsitem.headline: Traders think BoS intervening to stop peseta rise.

text.p: The Bank of Spain was believed to be intervening for the second time this week to halt the peseta's rise and was selling the currency at 84.05 against the mark, traders said on Thursday.
"The peseta reached the figure in Asia, but this morning someone has taken up all mark offers below 84.05, and it's very probably it was the Bank of Spain," said a trader.
The Bank of Spain declined to comment, as usual.

The peseta should have risen further on the back of lira strength and sustained demand for bonds, another trader said. But he added there were no concrete signs of the central bank's presence in the currency market.
The Bank of Spain was said to have intervened on Monday at the same level.
